solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mischievous about remaining beggar

indicators.note: the word for mischievous goes about, or around, the word for remaining

parts.note: impish means mischievous
over means left or remaining, as in 'food left over'

explanation.surface: A mischievous child hangs about while a beggar looks on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beggar' is a verb here, not the noun the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: To beggar someone is to reduce them to poverty, a synonym of making poor.

clue.text: Girl swallowing aluminium for a fever

indicators.note: the girl's name takes in the metal symbol, as if eating it

parts.note: Maria is a girl's name
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: A girl has swallowed some aluminium as a remedy for her fever.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaria is a mosquito-borne disease marked by recurring bouts of high temperature.

clue.text: Start on introducing exercises

indicators.note: the word on has the exercises brought into its middle

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: Someone begins a session by bringing in some exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is not a link word: its letters are split to take PE inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To open a meeting or a show is to begin it, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: English reputation lies initially in painted artwork

parts.note: a name is a reputation, as in 'making a name for yourself'

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word lies is taken

explanation.surface: An English artist's reputation turns out to rest on lies in a painted work.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamel work is decorative art made by fusing coloured glassy coatings onto metal, so a painted piece.

clue.text: I'm one who carries for international trader

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
a porter carries luggage or loads

explanation.surface: A person explains that they carry goods for a firm that trades abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A company that brings goods in from other countries to sell trades across borders.

clue.text: He will ring in greeting

parts.note: taken as written
'll is the contracted form of will, as in he'll
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A man promises to phone with a word of welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like a phone call but is the round letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the standard word said on meeting someone or answering a phone.

clue.text: Australian flyer has to shift equipment by air without one

parts.note: to budge is to move or shift
a rig is a set of equipment, such as a drilling rig

indicators.note: the letter for one is left out of the word air

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An Australian traveller must move gear by plane without a single piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flyer' suggests an aircraft passenger; it is a small parrot.
explanation.definitionFit: The budgie is a small parakeet native to Australia, a bird kept as a pet worldwide.

clue.text: Volcanic opening about to swallow tree

indicators.note: the short word for about takes the tree inside it, as if eating it

parts.note: ca, for circa, means about
the alder is a tree

explanation.surface: A volcano's mouth is on the point of engulfing a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the large crater formed when a volcano collapses after an eruption.

clue.text: Carriage driver's optimism about a public disturbance

indicators.note: the word for optimism goes around the other pieces

parts.note: cheer is good spirits or optimism
a riot is a violent public disturbance

explanation.surface: A coachman stays hopeful despite unrest in the streets.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of driver's stands for 'is' and joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient times the person driving a two-wheeled horse-drawn war or racing vehicle had this title.

clue.text: Spicy rice, alluring eastern cuisine (one wants seconds!)

definitions.text: Spicy rice, alluring eastern cuisine (one wants seconds!)

indicators.note: a diner asking for seconds here means taking the second letter of each word

explanation.surface: A tempting Asian rice dish so good you want another helping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seconds' looks like a second helping but picks letter two of each of the five words before the bracket.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a dish of rice cooked in stock with spices, common in Middle Eastern and South Asian cooking.

clue.text: Mediterranean port area

definitions.meaning: a port city on the coast of northern Israel, famous in the Crusades
a unit of land measure, about 4,047 square metres

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the Israeli harbour city; the other is the imperial unit for land area.

clue.text: Nearly go running through all four seasons

indicators.note: running suggests the letters are in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone almost goes jogging every season of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' is the anagram signal for NEARLY GO.
explanation.definitionFit: Spring, summer, autumn and winter together make up one complete year, so lasting through them is lasting a year.

clue.text: Sit awkwardly in ceremonial uniform in agony

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are placed inside the uniform word

parts.note: full dress, or dress uniform, is formal military uniform for ceremonies

indicators.note: sitting awkwardly suggests the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A soldier sits uncomfortably in parade uniform, suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'in' only links; the first is the insertion signal, and 'awkwardly' jumbles the three letters into ISTR before they go in.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean severe mental or physical suffering, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Type of children's book heroine mostly following it

indicators.note: the shortened name comes after the word it
most of the name is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: Alice is the heroine of Alice's Adventures in Wonderland

explanation.surface: A kind of storybook in which the heroine mostly follows something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Type of' looks like a link to the book, but Type alone is the definition, the printing sense.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the sloping typeface used for emphasis, a style of printed letters.

clue.text: Liven up by means of hot spice

parts.note: to pep something up is to liven it
per means by or through, as in 'per post'

explanation.surface: A cook adds life to a dish using something fiery.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground from peppercorns, this is a pungent seasoning found on most tables.

clue.text: Joke about girl being strictly moral

indicators.note: the joke word wraps around the girl's name

parts.note: a pun is a play on words, a type of joke
Rita is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone makes a joke about a girl for being so prim.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective it describes someone with rigid, austere standards of behaviour.

clue.text: All others in post office can be very quick

indicators.note: the word for the others goes inside the post office letters

parts.note: the rest means all the others

explanation.surface: Everyone else at the post office can move fast.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical direction meaning fast, also used of anything done in a flash.

clue.text: Understood vase is rarely open

parts.note: tacit means understood without being said
an urn is a vase-like vessel

explanation.surface: It goes without saying that a vase is seldom left uncovered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'open' looks to be about the vase's lid; it means talkative.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserved, uncommunicative person seldom speaks, so they rarely open their mouth or open up.

clue.text: Vegetable is cold and tough

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
hard means tough

explanation.surface: A vegetable left chilled has gone stiff.
explanation.definitionFit: Swiss chard is a leafy green eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Mist surrounding river amphibian

indicators.note: the mist word goes around the river abbreviation

parts.note: fog is thick mist
R is the abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: Mist hangs over a river where a creature lives.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a tailless amphibian that lives both in water and on land.

clue.text: Cover coolants regularly going missing

indicators.note: every other letter of coolants drops out, leaving the alternate ones

explanation.surface: An engine cover loses its coolant fluids every so often.
explanation.definitionFit: A coat of paint covers a surface, so a layer laid over is a covering.

clue.text: Rub out because put in before

indicators.note: the word for because is inserted into the word for before

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
as can mean because

explanation.surface: Someone deletes a mark because it was entered earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: To delete writing with an eraser is to remove it, a synonym phrase.

clue.text: Marksman getting small owl, perhaps

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
an owl is an example of something that hoots

explanation.surface: A sharpshooter bags what might be a little owl.
explanation.definitionFit: A marksman is someone who fires a gun skilfully.

clue.text: Rather sour tonic tends to go off

indicators.note: going off suggests spoiling and the letters being thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A drink of tonic tends to turn somewhat sour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go off' is the anagram signal for TONIC TENDS.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissatisfied person is soured, unhappy with their lot, so mildly bitter in mood.
